messages:
matt: Planning to pin provider + modules and take a workspace lock for the tenant-peering apply during the release quiet window tomorrow. Requesting deploybot hold and a 01:30-03:00 UTC window.

dalia: Acknowledge. Which pins + why?

matt: provider.aws=5.12.1, module.peering=v3.0.0-rc1 (we're avoiding the auto-route-refactor in main), module.nat=v1.9.2. This is to prevent unintended replacement of cross-account peering during the cutover.

tomas: Please also set TF_WORKSPACE=prod-tenant and lock state before plan. Small ask: add `terraform state list | grep aws_vpc_peering` check to preflight.

matt: Yep, plan will run under locked workspace. Preflight commands in playbook:```bash
export TF_WORKSPACE=prod-tenant
terraform init -input=false
terraform workspace select prod-tenant || terraform workspace new prod-tenant
terraform plan -var-file=prod.pin.tfvars -out=canary.plan
```

deploybot: Hold requested by matt for tenant-peering. Auto-merge paused. Use `deploybot hold --who=matt` to view.

ops-bot: NOTE: Running smoke preflight against staging canary now. Will post plan diff shortly.

(00:45 UTC) ops-bot: PREVIEW: plan shows 1 replace on aws_nat_gateway.nat-gw-azb if route-table association changes. Flagging for review.

dalia: Replace on nat-gw is a red flag. Why is TF planning replace? Should be an in-place update.

tomas: Likely due to changed `allocation_id` calculation from the new module.nat. Check provider pining first.
matt: I'll run `terraform plan -target=module.nat -var-file=prod.pin.tfvars` to isolate. Giving ops-bot the run.

(00:52 UTC) ops-bot: ISOLATED PLAN: module.nat intends to replace aws_nat_gateway.nat-gw-azb because attribute `subnet_id` will change (derived value).

dalia: Ok we cannot replace nat gateways during cutover. Abort apply. Unpin module.nat until we refactor allocation_id usage.
matt: Agreed. New plan: keep module.nat at v1.9.1, still pin provider.aws and module.peering. Update prod.pin.tfvars accordingly.

tomas: Also recommend we increase kube-probe timeout on tenant pods from 5s -> 10s in the canary so probes don't trigger during route updates. Add to playbook.

matt: I'll update the playbook and varfile. After that we'll re-run isolated plan for peering+provider only.

(01:20 UTC) ops-bot: NEW PLAN SUMMARY: 0 to add, 1 to change (module.peering - route table attribute), 0 to destroy. No nat-gw replacements. Hash: fed9c3.

dalia: Good. What's rollback plan if peering change causes route flaps?

matt: Rollback steps in playbook: 1) `deploybot rollback --target=tenant-peering --tag v2026-03-22-pre-pin` 2) revert routing via `aws ec2 replace-route` script (we've versioned previous route table) 3) scale down canary to 0 and restore old BGP sessions. Full commands are in the playbook snippet.

tomas: Add metric triggers: if BGP session flaps >3 times in 10m OR control-plane API 5xx >4% for 5m -> rollback.

deploybot: Rollout scheduled by matt for 2026-03-22T01:30:00Z. Canary policy: 25% traffic for 15m -> 50% 15m -> 100% if green. Auto-merge paused. Workspace locked.

matt: Running `terraform apply -var-file=prod.pin.tfvars -target=module.peering -auto-approve` in canary at 01:40 UTC, will paste output.

(01:41 UTC) matt: Apply succeeded for module.peering. Route table updated, canary switched to 25%. Plan hash: fed9c3.

(01:55 UTC) ops-bot: METRIC: Observed 2 BGP session flaps for tenant-peer-3 within 10m window but no control-plane errors. Monitor closely.

(02:05 UTC) dalia: Flaps subsided. BGP stable. Proceeding to 50% per policy.

(02:25 UTC) ops-bot: METRIC: Control-plane 5xx jumped to 4.6% for 6m. Threshold is 4% -> initiating recommended rollback.

(02:26 UTC) matt: Initiating rollback per metric trigger. Executing playbook rollback steps now.

(02:27 UTC) deploybot: Rollback initiated by matt -> target tenant-peering -> tag v2026-03-22-pre-pin. ETA ~4m.

(02:31 UTC) deploybot: Rollback complete. Workspace unlocked. Auto-merge still paused.

(02:33 UTC) tomas: Post-rollback verification: route tables restored, BGP sessions stable, control-plane errors dropping back to baseline within 3m.

(02:40 UTC) matt: We'll pause this change until refactor on module.nat and extra probe margins are in place. I'll file a follow-up ticket with timeline + lessons. Leaving the hold in place until I release it.

deploybot: Hold remains. Use `deploybot hold --release --who=matt` when ready to re-schedule.
